label: final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or <DEL>. The core is the last step of length-3 sequences (t=5: input orig(1), output orig(2)). That step holds 82% of activation mass and every top example; about 74% of those steps fire, and they make up 98% of the top activation quartile. A weak, low-magnitude tail fires on the last or second-to-last copy steps of longer sequences (L=4 at t=7, and L=9 at t=17), so recall by count is only about 0.56. It never fires on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=0 for every activation). It is somewhat stronger with no digits among the originals and when in_tok is m/h/o/i/n, but I did not find a clean rule for which L=3 final steps stay silent.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: m, h, o, n, i, r; least: y, w, c, l) and the first original token (most: n, g, q, p, 2, l; least: z, x, d, m); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=3, t=5.
